target_customer: Hospitals, imaging centers and radiology labs, mainly in Latin America and other emerging markets
problem: Radiology workflows (PACS, RIS, reporting) are fragmented and radiologists are scarce; the company's original idea (Higia) was breast cancer screening.
business_model: Cloud software subscription for imaging providers plus AI reporting tools (pricing not found)
product_category: Diagnostic OS: cloud PACS, RIS and AI radiology

founders.name: Julián Cantú
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says he was moved by his mother's cancer battles; a surname 'Ríos' also appears there.

technical_complexity.rationale: Cloud medical imaging and AI reading in 2018 needed integration with scanners and clinical validation; the original screening idea needed more regulatory depth.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration into clinical workflows and imaging archives creates lock-in once adopted.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying Eden; the company reports 2,800+ systems in 20 countries (self-reported).

market_need_then: Radiologist shortages and weak imaging software in Latin America; Axios (July 2024) framed the raise around the global radiologist shortage.

identity.voice_and_tone: 'Tools for Miracles' tagline on About page; mission language about medicine as humanity's most sacred work

rebrands.why: Not stated; follows a 2021 rebuild from breast cancer screening to radiology workflows per a directory profile

brand_strength.rationale: Tagline exists but no press on brand pull found; several unrelated companies share the name Eden.

pivots.why: A directory profile (healthcarediscovery.ai) states the rebuild began in Aug 2021; reason not given

outcome_analysis: Eden began as Higia, a breast cancer screening idea in S18, rebuilt around radiology software in 2021 and by 2025 reports serving 2,800+ health systems and raising a $22M Series A. The pivot into infrastructure software seems to be what unlocked growth; funding totals and several rounds are inconsistent across sources, so scale claims are largely company-reported.
notes: Total raised conflicts: $44M, $48.7M, $53.32M across aggregators. The $10M July 2024 round was led by Sierra Ventures; one outlet frames the $22M as including it, so stage of the 2024 round is uncertain and recorded as other. Earlier Sierra Ventures early-stage investment page exists but amount and date not extracted. HQ differs: San Francisco (YC), Mexico City, Sao Paulo. Founders' prior jobs not found. Competition: no dated sources found.
